record.paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For the Cauchy problem on the real line for the fourth-order degenerate thin-film equation with compactly supported nonnegative initial data and mobility depending on a power of h, do weak solutions converge as time grows to the corresponding source-type self-similar solution?

evidence.quote: convergence onto the source type solution for the CAUCHY problem on the line

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Cauchy problem on the real line for the fourth-order degenerate thin-film equation
\[
\partial_t h + \partial_x\!\big(h^{n}\,\partial_x^{3} h\big) = 0, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},\ t>0,
\]
where $n>0$ is a fixed exponent (mobility $m(h)=h^{n}$), with nonnegative, compactly supported initial datum $h_0\in L^{1}(\mathbb{R})$ of finite mass $M=\int_{\mathbb{R}} h_0\,dx>0$. Let $h(\cdot,t)\ge 0$ denote a weak (e.g. energy/entropy) solution preserving mass. For each admissible $n$ there exists a unique nonnegative, compactly supported, mass-$M$ self-similar source-type solution of the form
\[
h_*(x,t)=t^{-\alpha}\,F\!\big(x\,t^{-\alpha}\big),\qquad \alpha=\tfrac{1}{n+4},
\]
where $F$ is the corresponding self-similar profile.

Question: For every admissible $n>0$, does the weak solution $h(\cdot,t)$ converge as $t\to\infty$ to the source-type self-similar solution $h_*(\cdot,t)$ of the same mass (in a suitable norm, e.g. $L^1(\mathbb{R})$, after rescaling to self-similar variables)?
artifact.status_search_result: For the linear-mobility case n=1, convergence of strong/entropy solutions with compactly supported initial data on the real line to the unique source-type self-similar profile has been proved (Carrillo–Toscani; Carlen–Ulusoy), with explicit (slow) rates in L^1 and H^1 via asymptotic equipartition of the excess energy. For general mobility exponents n and for general weak solutions, the question is not fully settled; results are available only in restricted regimes, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic equipartition and long time behavior of solutions of a thin-film equation
status_evidence.snippet: For the classical thin film Cauchy problem on the whole real line, asymptotic equipartition is used to show H¹(ℝ) convergence of solutions to the unique self-similar solution.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence of strong solutions to the source-type self-similar solution is established for the linear-mobility thin-film equation on R.

status_evidence.title: Long-Time Asymptotics for Strong Solutions of the Thin Film Equation
status_evidence.snippet: strong solutions relax in the L¹(ℝ) norm at an explicit rate to the unique self-similar source type solution with the same mass
status_evidence.claim: L^1 convergence to the source-type self-similar solution is known in specific (strong-solution, linear-mobility) settings.
